sql.def: Structured Query Language — the language used to ask a relational database for data (SELECT) or change it (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

table.def: A grid of rows and columns inside a database. Each row is one record (e.g. one customer); each column is one attribute (e.g. email).

row.def: One record in a table — a single horizontal entry.

column.def: One attribute in a table — a single vertical field shared by every row.

primary-key.def: A column (or set of columns) that uniquely identifies each row. Often an integer ID like customer_id.

index.def: A side data structure that lets the database find rows by a column quickly, instead of scanning the whole table. Trade-off: faster reads, slightly slower writes.

transaction.def: A group of SQL statements treated as one unit: either all succeed (COMMIT) or none take effect (ROLLBACK).

acid.def: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the four guarantees a relational database provides for transactions.

isolation.def: How much one transaction can see of another transaction's in-progress changes. MySQL's default is REPEATABLE READ — your transaction sees a consistent snapshot.

mvcc.def: Multi-Version Concurrency Control. InnoDB keeps old versions of rows so readers don't block writers and vice versa.

innodb.def: The default storage engine inside MySQL. It actually stores the rows on disk, manages B+ trees, and provides ACID guarantees.

btree.def: The tree-shaped data structure InnoDB uses for indexes. Internal nodes store key ranges; leaf nodes store rows. Lookups are roughly log(N).

binlog.def: A log file MySQL writes for every change. Other MySQLs read it to replicate. Vitess's VReplication reads it to copy or transform data.

gtid.def: Global Transaction ID. A unique name for every transaction, so a replica can ask any source 'give me everything after GTID X'.

replication.def: Copying changes from one MySQL ('primary') to one or more 'replicas' so they have a near-real-time copy of the data.

primary.def: The MySQL that accepts writes. Other MySQLs replicate from it. Sometimes called 'source' or historically 'master'.

replica.def: A read-only MySQL that follows a primary. If the primary dies, one replica is promoted.

semi-sync.def: Variant of replication where the primary waits for at least one replica to acknowledge receipt of an event before saying COMMIT succeeded. Reduces data loss on failover.

mysqld.def: The actual MySQL server process — a binary called 'mysqld' that listens on port 3306.

wire-protocol.def: The exact bytes a MySQL client and server exchange. Vitess implements both ends in go/mysql/.

pool.def: A reusable set of open database connections. Opening a connection is slow; a pool lets many requests share a small number of long-lived connections.

vitess.def: An open-source layer on top of MySQL that adds sharding, automated failover, online schema changes, and a unified entry point for apps.

vtgate.def: Vitess's stateless query router. Apps connect to it as if it were a single MySQL; vtgate plans queries and routes them to the right shards.

vttablet.def: A Vitess sidecar process colocated with each mysqld. It handles connection pooling, query rewriting, transactions, schema tracking, and reports health to vtgate.

vtctld.def: Vitess's control-plane daemon. Operators talk to it (via vtctldclient) to create keyspaces, reshard, take backups, run online DDL, etc.

vtctldclient.def: Command-line tool that sends RPCs to vtctld. The everyday admin CLI.

vtorc.def: Vitess's failover daemon. Watches replication topology and triggers a reparent if the primary dies.

topo.def: A small distributed configuration store (etcd / ZooKeeper / consul) that holds the cluster's shape: keyspaces, shards, tablets, vschema, routing rules.

cell.def: One failure domain in Vitess — usually a datacenter or availability zone. Each cell has its own local topo.

keyspace.def: A logical database in Vitess. Contains tables. Can be unsharded (one shard) or sharded (multiple shards).

shard.def: One slice of a sharded keyspace. Has its own primary + replicas. Named by its key range, e.g. '-80' or '80-c0'.

keyrange.def: The hex range a shard covers. '-80' means [00, 80); '80-' means [80, FF]. Together they tile the whole 8-byte space.

keyspace-id.def: An 8-byte value that decides which shard a row lives on. Computed from a row's column value via a vindex.

vindex.def: Vitess Index — a function that maps a column value (like customer_id) to a keyspace ID (and therefore to a shard). Examples: hash, lookup, xxhash.

vschema.def: The Vitess-side schema config that tells vtgate which tables in a keyspace are sharded, by which column, and via which vindex.

vreplication.def: Vitess's data-movement engine. Tails one tablet's binlog and applies the rows on another. Powers MoveTables, Reshard, Materialize, OnlineDDL.

movetables.def: A Vitess workflow that copies tables from one keyspace to another, then switches traffic over. Built on VReplication.

reshard.def: A Vitess workflow that splits or merges shards within a keyspace. Built on VReplication.

vdiff.def: A Vitess tool that compares rows on the source and target of a VReplication workflow to confirm they match before cutover.

switchtraffic.def: The cutover step that moves reads (then writes) from the source of a workflow to the target. Reversible until you 'complete' the workflow.

online-ddl.def: Schema changes (ALTER TABLE) that happen in the background without blocking application traffic. In Vitess, often done via a VReplication-backed shadow table.

throttler.def: An in-process service in vttablet that tells background work (VReplication, OnlineDDL) to back off when replication is lagging.

ers.def: The 'primary is dead' failover. Vitess picks the most-advanced replica, promotes it, and re-parents the others. Triggered by vtorc.

prs.def: A controlled failover used during maintenance. Old primary is still alive; we drain its writes, promote a chosen replica, and update topo.

rpc.def: Remote Procedure Call — one process calls a function on another over the network. Vitess uses gRPC for almost all internal RPCs.

grpc.def: A framework for typed RPCs over HTTP/2. Vitess defines services in .proto files under proto/, then generates Go code.

protobuf.def: Protocol Buffers — Google's typed serialization format. Vitess's wire schemas and topo records are protobufs.

ast.def: Abstract Syntax Tree. The structured representation of parsed SQL — nodes for SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, etc. Lives in go/vt/sqlparser/.

planner.def: The vtgate component that turns parsed SQL (AST) into a plan — a tree of execution primitives that decide which shards to hit and how to combine results.

primitive.def: An execution step inside a vtgate plan: Route, Join, Aggregate, Limit, etc. Lives in go/vt/vtgate/engine/.

sysvars.def: MySQL session and global settings (e.g. character_set_client). Vitess intercepts SETs and may pass them through to backends.

backup.def: A snapshot of a mysqld's data files plus a binlog position. Used to disaster-recover or to spin up new replicas.

restore.def: Reconstruct a tablet's data from a backup, then replay binlogs to catch up to 'now'.

goroutine.def: A lightweight thread of execution in Go. Vitess uses many of them — one per RPC, one per VReplication stream, etc.

context.def: Go's idiomatic way to carry deadlines, cancellation, and trace info through a call chain. Every long-running Vitess function takes a Context as its first argument.

interface.def: A named set of method signatures. Anything that has those methods automatically implements the interface — no 'implements' keyword needed.
